description: Use when a Rust release build in CI is killed during the final link step (signal 9, exit code 137, or "ld terminated") because the runner ran out of memory
when_to_use: Large crates built with LTO and many codegen units can exhaust a small CI runner's RAM while linking, so the job dies without a compiler error.
procedure: Confirm the kill in the job log: exit code 137 or SIGKILL right after the last crate compiles.
Use thin LTO (`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=thin`) or raise `codegen-units` for CI builds.
Limit parallelism with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` so rustc and the linker do not compete for memory.
Switch to a leaner linker such as lld or mold via `-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=lld`.
pitfalls: Full debug info for dependencies inflates link memory; set `debug = "line-tables-only"` in the release profile.
A bigger runner hides the problem until the binary grows again.
verification: Re-run the job and compare peak memory in the runner metrics; the link step must finish with exit code 0.

description: Use when a Rust crate compiles on its own but fails or behaves differently inside the workspace because Cargo unifies dependency features across members of the parent workspace
when_to_use: `cargo build -p member` and `cargo build --workspace` disagree, or a dependency feature is enabled that the crate never requested.
procedure: Run `cargo tree -e features -i <dependency>` to see which member turns the feature on.
Set `resolver = "2"` in the parent workspace `Cargo.toml` so build and dev dependency features stay separate.
Declare every feature a crate relies on explicitly instead of inheriting it from a sibling.
Check each member alone with `cargo check -p <member>` in CI.
pitfalls: Edition 2021 crates default to resolver 2, but a virtual workspace manifest still needs it set explicitly.
`cargo hack --each-feature` is slow on large workspaces; run it nightly.
verification: `cargo check -p <member>` and `cargo check --workspace` both succeed with the same feature set reported by `cargo tree`.

description: Use when `pip install -e .` succeeds but importing the package fails with ModuleNotFoundError, typically in a src/ layout project with a misconfigured pyproject.toml
when_to_use: The package code lives under `src/`, the editable install reports success, and `import mypackage` still fails outside the repository root.
procedure: Inspect `pyproject.toml` and confirm the build backend knows about the `src` directory (for setuptools: `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] where = ["src"]`).
Make sure the package directory contains an `__init__.py` or is configured as a namespace package.
Reinstall with `pip install -e . --no-build-isolation -v` and read which packages were discovered.
Run `python -c 'import mypackage, sys; print(mypackage.__file__)'` from a different directory.
pitfalls: Running from the repository root can mask the problem because the current directory is on `sys.path`.
Old `.egg-link` files from previous installs shadow the new editable finder.
verification: The import works from `/tmp` and `__file__` points into the `src/` tree.

description: Use when a package is installed with pip but `python` still cannot import it because a different interpreter or virtual environment is active
when_to_use: `pip install` reports success or "Requirement already satisfied" while `python` raises ModuleNotFoundError for the same package.
procedure: Compare `which python`, `which pip`, and `python -m pip --version`.
Always install with `python -m pip install <package>` so pip matches the interpreter.
Activate the project virtual environment, or point the editor's interpreter setting at `.venv/bin/python`.
Recreate the environment if it was copied from another machine or Python version.
pitfalls: Shell aliases and pyenv shims can make `pip` and `python` resolve to different installations.
IDEs cache the interpreter choice per workspace.
verification: `python -m pip show <package>` lists a location inside the active environment and the import succeeds.

description: Use when `npm ci` fails in CI saying package.json and package-lock.json are not in sync, or the lockfile was created by a different npm version
when_to_use: The install step of a pipeline stops with `npm ci can only install packages when your package.json and package-lock.json are in sync`.
procedure: Run `npm install` locally with the same npm major version the CI uses to regenerate the lockfile.
Commit `package-lock.json` together with the `package.json` change.
Pin the npm version in CI (for example with `corepack` or `actions/setup-node`) to match local development.
Re-run `npm ci` locally on a clean checkout before pushing.
pitfalls: Switching CI to `npm install` hides the drift instead of fixing it.
Lockfile version 1 vs 3 differences come from npm 6 vs npm 7+.
verification: `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` succeeds locally and in the pipeline.

description: Use when Node.js throws ERR_REQUIRE_ESM or "Cannot use import statement outside a module" when mixing CommonJS and ES modules
when_to_use: A dependency upgrade turned a package ESM-only, or a file uses `import` syntax while Node treats it as CommonJS.
procedure: Decide the project's module system: set `"type": "module"` in `package.json` or keep CommonJS.
In CommonJS code, load ESM-only packages with dynamic `await import()` instead of `require()`.
Rename files to `.mjs` or `.cjs` when a single file must differ from the package default.
Align the TypeScript `module` and `moduleResolution` settings with the chosen system.
pitfalls: Pinning the dependency to its last CommonJS major only postpones the migration.
Jest needs its own ESM configuration even when Node runs the code fine.
verification: `node` starts the entry point without module errors and the test runner passes.

description: Use when a Postgres query is slow in production and you need to read EXPLAIN ANALYZE output to find a sequential scan and add the right index
when_to_use: A query's latency grew with table size and the plan is unknown.
procedure: Run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on the exact query with realistic parameters.
Look for `Seq Scan` nodes on large tables and big gaps between estimated and actual rows.
Create a matching index with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on the filtered and sorted columns.
Run `ANALYZE` on the table if estimates are far off.
pitfalls: `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` executes the statement; wrap writes in a transaction and roll back.
An index on a low-selectivity column is often ignored by the planner.
verification: The new plan uses an index scan and the measured execution time drops.

description: Use when the application fails with "sorry, too many clients already" or connection timeouts against Postgres under load
when_to_use: Errors appear only under traffic peaks or after scaling out application instances.
procedure: Count connections per client with `SELECT usename, application_name, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY 1, 2`.
Size each instance's pool so instances times pool size stays below `max_connections` minus a reserve.
Put PgBouncer in transaction pooling mode in front of the database for many short-lived clients.
Close leaked connections: look for long `idle in transaction` sessions.
pitfalls: Raising `max_connections` costs memory per backend and usually moves the bottleneck.
Transaction pooling breaks session features such as prepared statements and advisory locks.
verification: A load test at peak traffic runs without connection errors and `pg_stat_activity` stays below the limit.

description: Use when a Kubernetes pod is stuck in CrashLoopBackOff and you need the previous container's logs, exit code, and the reason it keeps restarting
when_to_use: `kubectl get pods` shows a growing restart count and the current logs are empty.
procedure: Read the crashed container's output with `kubectl logs <pod> --previous`.
Check `kubectl describe pod <pod>` for the last state, exit code, and `OOMKilled` reason.
Verify the command, environment variables, and mounted secrets the container expects.
If the probe kills it, relax the liveness probe's `initialDelaySeconds`.
pitfalls: Exit code 137 means the kernel killed the process, usually for exceeding its memory limit.
Events expire after an hour; capture them early.
verification: The pod reaches `Running` and the restart count stops increasing.

description: Use when Kubernetes pods stay in ImagePullBackOff or ErrImagePull, usually a wrong image tag or missing credentials for a private registry
when_to_use: New pods never start and `kubectl describe pod` shows pull failures.
procedure: Read the exact pull error in the pod events (`not found`, `unauthorized`, or a timeout).
Confirm the image reference and tag exist with `docker manifest inspect <image>`.
Create a docker-registry secret and reference it in `imagePullSecrets` or the service account.
Check node egress to the registry for timeouts.
pitfalls: Secrets are namespaced; the pull secret must live in the pod's namespace.
The `latest` tag plus `IfNotPresent` can keep stale images on some nodes.
verification: The pod events show `Successfully pulled image` and the pod starts.

description: Use when terraform plan or apply fails with "Error acquiring the state lock" after an interrupted run left a stale lock in the remote backend
when_to_use: A previous run was cancelled or crashed and every new run now waits on or fails at the lock.
procedure: Confirm nobody else is running terraform against the same state (check CI and teammates).
Copy the lock ID from the error message.
Run `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` from the same working directory and backend configuration.
Re-run `terraform plan` and review it before applying.
pitfalls: Force-unlocking while another apply is running can corrupt the state.
For DynamoDB-backed locks, deleting the item by hand skips the safety checks.
verification: `terraform plan` acquires the lock and finishes without lock errors.

description: Use when a GitHub Actions workflow never restores its dependency cache and every run downloads and reinstalls everything from scratch
when_to_use: The cache step logs `Cache not found for input keys` on every run, including reruns of the same commit.
procedure: Build the key from a hash of the lockfile: `key: ${{ runner.os }}-deps-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}`.
Add `restore-keys` with the key prefix so a partial match is restored.
Make sure the cached path is the real download directory of the package manager.
Remember caches are scoped to the branch and its base branch.
pitfalls: Caches created on a pull request branch are not visible to other branches.
Including a timestamp or run number in the key guarantees a miss.
verification: The second run of the workflow logs `Cache restored from key` and the install step is faster.

description: Use when a GitHub Actions job gets 403 "Resource not accessible by integration" while pushing a tag, creating a release, or commenting on a pull request
when_to_use: A workflow step that writes to the repository fails with 403 although it works for maintainers locally.
procedure: Add a `permissions:` block to the job granting only what it needs, such as `contents: write` or `pull-requests: write`.
Check the repository's default workflow permissions under Settings, Actions.
For pull requests from forks, use `pull_request_target` carefully or post results from a separate workflow.
Use a fine-grained token only when `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot be granted the scope.
pitfalls: A top-level `permissions:` block replaces all defaults, so unlisted scopes become `none`.
`pull_request_target` with a checkout of untrusted code is a security risk.
verification: The job's step succeeds and the tag, release, or comment appears.

description: Use when browsers accept the HTTPS site but curl, Java, or Android clients fail certificate verification because nginx serves an incomplete chain
when_to_use: Desktop browsers work (they fetch missing intermediates themselves) while strict clients report `unable to get local issuer certificate`.
procedure: Inspect the served chain with `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host -showcerts`.
Point `ssl_certificate` at the full chain file (leaf followed by intermediates), not the leaf alone.
Reload nginx with `nginx -t && nginx -s reload`.
Re-test from a strict client.
pitfalls: Do not include the root certificate; clients already have it.
Certificate order matters: leaf first.
verification: `openssl s_client` reports `Verify return code: 0 (ok)` and curl succeeds without `-k`.

description: Use when WebSocket connections behind an nginx reverse proxy fail the upgrade with 400 or drop after about 60 seconds
when_to_use: Real-time features work against the app server directly but not through nginx.
procedure: Set `proxy_http_version 1.1;` in the location block.
Forward the handshake headers: `proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;` and `proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";`.
Raise `proxy_read_timeout` above the application's heartbeat interval.
Reload nginx and retest.
pitfalls: A load balancer in front of nginx may have its own idle timeout.
Hard-coding `Connection upgrade` for every request breaks keepalive; use a `map` on `$http_upgrade`.
verification: The browser's network tab shows `101 Switching Protocols` and the connection stays open past the old timeout.

description: Use when go get or go mod tidy fails for a private repository with 410 Gone, a checksum database error, or "terminal prompts disabled"
when_to_use: Public modules download fine but an internal module path cannot be fetched.
procedure: Set `GOPRIVATE=git.example.com/*` (go env -w) so the proxy and checksum database are skipped for those paths.
Configure git to use SSH or a credential helper for the host: `git config --global url."git@host:".insteadOf https://host/`.
Run `go mod tidy` again.
Set the same variables in CI.
pitfalls: `GONOSUMDB` alone still sends requests through the public proxy.
Module paths are case sensitive.
verification: `go mod download` succeeds on a clean module cache.

description: Use when environment variables are undefined in the generated production bundle of a React app built with Vite or Create React App, although they work in dev
when_to_use: Values read from `import.meta.env` or `process.env` are undefined only after a production build or deploy.
procedure: Prefix exposed variables correctly: `VITE_` for Vite, `REACT_APP_` for Create React App.
Make sure the variables exist at build time in the CI job, not only at container runtime.
Rebuild; values are inlined into the bundle during the build.
For runtime configuration, serve a small `config.json` instead.
pitfalls: Never expose secrets this way: everything inlined is public in the bundle.
Changing the variable in the hosting dashboard has no effect until the next build.
verification: Search the built assets for the expected value or log it in the deployed app.

description: Use when git over SSH fails with "Permission denied (publickey)" or ssh asks for the key passphrase on every connection
when_to_use: A key exists in `~/.ssh` but the SSH client does not offer it, or offers it without a running agent.
procedure: Check what is offered with `ssh -vT git@github.com`.
Start the agent (`eval "$(ssh-agent -s)"`) and add the key with `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
Add a `Host` entry in `~/.ssh/config` with `IdentityFile` and `AddKeysToAgent yes`.
Make sure the public key is registered on the server or forge account.
pitfalls: Private key files must have mode 600 or ssh ignores them.
Too many keys in the agent can exhaust the server's authentication attempts.
verification: `ssh -T git@github.com` greets the user and `git fetch` works without a passphrase prompt.

description: Use when macOS refuses to open a downloaded command-line binary because the developer "cannot be verified" or the app "is damaged"
when_to_use: A binary downloaded through a browser is blocked by Gatekeeper on first run.
procedure: Confirm the attribute with `xattr -l <binary>` (look for `com.apple.quarantine`).
Remove it for a trusted binary with `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <binary>`.
Alternatively allow it once from System Settings, Privacy and Security.
Prefer installing through a package manager, which avoids the quarantine flag.
pitfalls: Only do this for binaries from a source you trust and whose checksum you verified.
Apple silicon also requires the binary to be at least ad-hoc signed.
verification: The binary runs and prints its version without a Gatekeeper dialog.

description: Use when a shell script checked out on Windows fails in a Linux container with "bad interpreter" or "$'\r': command not found" because of CRLF line endings in the file format
when_to_use: A script that runs on Linux machines fails only when the repository was checked out on Windows, often as a container entrypoint.
procedure: Confirm CRLF endings with `file script.sh` or `cat -A script.sh`.
Add `*.sh text eol=lf` to `.gitattributes` and renormalize with `git add --renormalize .`.
Convert existing files with `dos2unix` or the editor's line-ending setting.
Rebuild the image.
pitfalls: `core.autocrlf=true` on Windows reintroduces CRLF on checkout unless `.gitattributes` overrides it.
The error can surface as `no such file or directory` for the shebang interpreter.
verification: `file script.sh` no longer mentions CRLF and the container starts.

description: Use when tests pass when run alone but fail intermittently in the full suite or in parallel because they share global state, ports, or files
when_to_use: Failures depend on test order or concurrency rather than on the code under test.
procedure: Reproduce by running the suite repeatedly with a fixed random order seed and with parallelism on and off.
Bisect to the pair of tests that interfere.
Give each test its own temporary directory, database, and ephemeral port.
Reset global singletons and environment variables in teardown.
pitfalls: Retrying flaky tests automatically hides real races.
Fixed sleeps make tests slower and still flaky.
verification: The suite passes 20 consecutive runs in parallel with randomized order.

description: Use when pytest tests pass individually but fail when the whole file runs because a module- or session-scoped fixture leaks mutated state
when_to_use: A test fails only after another test in the same module or session modified a shared fixture object.
procedure: List fixture scopes with `pytest --setup-show`.
Narrow the scope of the mutated fixture to `function`, or return a fresh copy each time.
Use `monkeypatch` and `tmp_path` instead of editing globals or shared directories.
Run with `pytest -p no:randomly` and then with random order to confirm the fix.
pitfalls: A session-scoped database fixture needs a transaction rollback per test.
Autouse fixtures in `conftest.py` apply to more tests than expected.
verification: The whole file passes in any order, including with `pytest-randomly`.

description: Use when a service started with docker compose gets "permission denied" writing to a bind-mounted volume, or leaves root-owned files on the host
when_to_use: The container user and the host user have different UIDs and the service writes into a bind mount.
procedure: Compare `id` on the host with `docker compose exec <service> id`.
Run the service as the host user with `user: "${UID}:${GID}"` in the compose file.
Or create the directory with the right owner in the image and use a named volume.
Fix files already owned by root with `sudo chown -R $USER .`.
pitfalls: `UID` is a shell variable, not always exported; pass it via `.env` for compose.
SELinux hosts also need the `:z` mount suffix.
verification: The service writes to the mount and new files on the host belong to the host user.

description: Use when outbound HTTP requests hang forever or fail on transient 502/503 errors and the client needs explicit timeouts and retries with backoff
when_to_use: Calls to an external API block workers indefinitely or fail on short upstream outages.
procedure: Set separate connect and read timeouts on the client; most libraries default to none.
Retry only idempotent requests on connection errors, 502, 503, and 504.
Use exponential backoff with jitter and a cap on attempts.
Honor `Retry-After` headers when the server sends them.
pitfalls: Retrying non-idempotent POSTs can duplicate side effects; use idempotency keys.
Retries across several layers multiply the load during an outage.
verification: A test against a stub server that delays or returns 503 finishes within the expected time budget.

description: Use when an app ignores an environment variable you set because a .env file or config file value silently takes precedence over it
when_to_use: Exporting a variable in the shell or deployment has no effect on the running application.
procedure: Find where configuration is loaded and in what order (defaults, config file, `.env`, environment, flags).
Check whether the dotenv loader overrides existing variables (for example `override=True`).
Make the environment win over files, and document the precedence order.
Print the effective configuration at startup, with secrets masked.
pitfalls: A `.env` file committed to the image overrides deployment settings silently.
Variable names may be prefixed or upper-cased by the config library.
verification: Setting the variable changes the value in the startup configuration log.

description: Use when npm install fails with ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree because of conflicting peer dependencies
when_to_use: Deprecated: forcing `--legacy-peer-deps` hides real version conflicts.
procedure: Run `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`.
Commit an `.npmrc` with `legacy-peer-deps=true`.
pitfalls: Peer conflicts surface later as runtime errors.
verification: `npm install` completes.
